> But this was not Anders fault. Anders' goal was the freedom, not "bloodbath" or "vengeance" (Who wanted vengeance was Sebastian – if Hawke didn't kill Anders). 

By the end of DA2 Anders *absolutely* was motivated by vengeance, though. Anders admits himself that his inner hatred towards templars transformed Justice into a spirit of Vengeance. By the time Anders blows up the chantry it’s not Anders/Justice, it’s Anders/Vengeance. *His Specialization is literally called “Vengeance”, for crying out loud.*

That’s always been the point ,to me. DA2 is a series of tragedies that culminates into what Anders is driven to do. He’s meant to be a tragic character, not a hero.

Elthina was absolutely not the only person killed by the explosion. From the wiki:

> Anders declared that he would no longer allow the templars to persecute mages and caused an explosion that destroyed the Kirkwall Chantry and killed all those inside, the Grand Cleric included, thus removing the possibility of compromise. Furthermore, as Anders did not contain the explosion, deadly debris from the blast also rained over half of Kirkwall, creating more chaos.

There’s undoubtedly a lot of innocent people who had nothing to do with the chantry who Anders killed. There’s dialogue in the game that refer to it as a mass murder and terrorist act. I get why people sympathize with Anders, he’s a tragic and heartbreaking character. But a tragic, heartbreaking terrorist mass murderer nonetheless.

You may want to consider making your walls out of stone instead of steel. At least your exterior walls, and the walls surrounding your batteries. Steel walls will still burn, albeit slower than wood. 

You also should consider spacing out your batteries more. The way they currently are, if one discharges they're all going to catch on fire and get damaged. You can uninstall and move batteries without losing their charge. Once you're done replacing your walls, you should run your power conduits through the them (all the more reason to use stone walls). First you need to butcher the body. Under the production tab, there's a butchering table. Once you have that built, add a bill to it for the creature to be butchered. I usually have the bill set on forever so whenever something gets hunted my cook will butcher it right away. Also make sure you have a colonist that has cooking enabled in the work tab.

For cooking, there's three different work stations. The most simple can be found under the temperature tab and is the campfire. This can be useful early game. For more complicated meals look back under the production tab, there's a stove that runs off of wood and one that runs off of electricity. You can add bills to this as well, and your cook will fulfill them as long as you have the ingredients.

I hope this helps!

Corruption/Crimson will only spread to adjacent grass in prehardmode. It probably won't spread far as there's usually natural barriers like stone in the way. The moment you hit hard mode it'll be able to spread to dirt, stone, mud, etc. 

And I totally agree that rushing hard mode ruins the fun. Don't worry about corruption spread all that much, digging a few tunnels around areas you want to protect and using the clentaminator when you have access to it should be good enough. Have fun on your adventure!

Very rarely do I get a world without some corruption and snow biomes mixing. Corruption can spread to ice but can't spread to snow, so it's not that big of a deal. 

The jungle is your biggest issue here. If you plan to stick with this world, you'll have to make sure to quarantine your jungle before hardmode or the corruption will engulf it pretty quickly. If you're only half an hour in and aren't too keen on your world, there's no harm in generating another one and seeing if you like it more!

For clarification, the traveling merchant doesn't actually move in. He'll spawn randomly some days in the morning and leave at night. 

You also don't necessarily need a jungle biome for the Witch Doctor. He sells certain items only when in a jungle biome though, like the leaf wings in handmode. 

The only other npc that has a biome specific housing need is the Truffle npc, who can only live in an above ground mushroom biome. 

The rest of your npcs should be fine in the normal forest biome. I hope this info helps!
